Experiencing the same issue, occurs on both 1.15.9 and 1.15.10 (and likely a couple version earlier).

As it turns out, it freezes because it's waiting for Git to load all the changes made, specifically in the "Review panel".

**Quick Fix:** Use the couple seconds of lag-free time you have at the start to "Toggle Review" off (top-right corner, or press CTRL+Shift+R).

If you wait several minutes for Git to load all the changes, you'll have access to the app again and it won't freeze.
If you press "Toggle Review", to turn it on again. It'll immediately freeze the app (no leeway like last time), but again (after Git loads it all, you get full access to the desktop app again).

This only occurs with the "Review" panel's "Git changes", not the "N changes" from the "File tree" panel. And this is because the "Review" panel loads all the file change file content, every single one... despite the default being "Collapse All".

**Solution:** It should load/fetch for context, only when the user expands a file (which means, this sort lag occurs only occurs when you click "Expand all", and thus... the lag is expected), and the 'Review changes' panel should always being closed on start up.

>

> 
>     * OpenCode 1.15.5
> 
>     * No multiplexers (tmux/zellij)
>

I just did a debugging session with opencode and Big Pickle running outside of my project, I only received the error from within the project and only when my opencode.json file included an instructions entry. 

Root cause: opencode v1.15.10 has a regression in the instructions file parser — any # character in the instructions file causes the server to crash during initialization (config.providers, provider.list, app.agents, config.get all fail).

Thanks, this does overlap with the existing symbol/LSP issues, but I think it still adds a few distinct pieces of evidence that may help narrow the root cause.

Overlap with existing issues:
- #18610: same `debug lsp symbols` symptom; no LSP bootstrap, immediate empty result
- #27650: same `/find/symbol` symptom; empty result from the public API path
- #15314: similar class of LSP symbol/bootstrap issues across a different server/language

What seems new here:
- `debug lsp document-symbols` reproducibly sends `textDocument/documentSymbol` before the document is opened/added, which matches the observed `clangd` error: `trying to get AST for non-added document`
- `/find/symbol` was probed in a fresh server instance with logs captured before/after; it produced no visible LSP lifecycle events at all (`spawned lsp server`, `initialize`, `didOpen`, `workspace/symbol`, `serverID=clangd`)
- binary-level strings from the packaged executable suggest:
  - `documentSymbol(uri)` directly sends `textDocument/documentSymbol`
  - `workspaceSymbol(query)` iterates existing clients only
  - the internal non-public `lsp` tool path checks `hasClients(filePath)` before `touchFile(filePath, "document")`

So my current read is that there are probably two closely related issues here:
1. `document-symbols` has a request-order bug
2. symbol-search paths (`debug lsp symbols`, `/find/symbol`, and likely related internal wrappers) assume pre-existing client state instead of reliably bootstrapping it

If maintainers prefer, I am happy for this to be treated as a consolidation/reference issue linked to #18610 and #27650 rather than a completely separate bug.

I can reproduce a related case and have evidence that at least one failure mode is not a subagent/tool-completion UI issue, but a no-first-byte stall on the ChatGPT Codex backend path.

Environment:

- opencode `1.15.10`
- macOS
- ChatGPT OAuth / Codex subscription path
- provider/model: `openai/gpt-5.5`
- endpoint involved: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

Observed real failure:

- An opencode request started at `2026-05-24 14:34:40 UTC`.
- No assistant part / SSE event was recorded for about 29.5 minutes.
- The first attempt eventually returned Cloudflare `504 Gateway time-out`.
- `cf-ray`: `a00d05c65f818bcf-SIN`
- opencode then retried and the same message completed within a few seconds.

Important detail: this was before tool execution. The stuck period was waiting for the model stream to begin, not waiting for a tool call or subagent callback.

I extracted the failed request body from the opencode log and replayed it directly against `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`, bypassing opencode UI, MCP tool execution, and subagent completion logic.

Sanitized shape of the replayed request:

- body size: about `265 KB`
- input items: `46`
- tools: `43`
- tools JSON size: about `60 KB`
- includes `reasoning.encrypted_content`
- uses opencode's normal session/cache affinity shape:
  - `x-session-affinity: <session id>`
  - `session_id: <session id>`
  - body `prompt_cache_key: <session id>`

Reproduction result:

- Single replay usually succeeds in a few seconds.
- Concurrent replay is intermittent:
  - On one network: `3/4` direct replays completed in about `4-7s`; `1/4` received `0 bytes` for `60s` and hit the probe timeout.
  - After switching to mobile data: `3/4` completed in about `4-5.5s`; `1/4` again received `0 bytes` for `60s`.

This also does not look like a general local network problem:

- On mobile data, ordinary endpoints were fast:
  - `api.openai.com/v1/responses`: TTFB about `0.34s`
  - `openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`: TTFB about `0.21s`
  - `chatgpt.com/cdn-cgi/trace`: TTFB about `0.08s`
- But a lightweight request to `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` could complete TLS in about `50ms` and then receive `0 bytes` until client timeout.
- Both broadband and mobile landed on Cloudflare `SIN`.

My current conclusion:

This specific failure mode is a no-first-byte upstream stall on the ChatGPT Codex backend path, likely around Cloudflare/ChatGPT Codex backend/session-affinity/prompt-cache routing. It is not caused by tool execution itself. opencode makes it user-visible because orchestrator/subagent flows issue concurrent Codex requests and use a stable session id as affinity/cache key.

Client-side mitigations that would help even if the upstream is the root cause:

- Add/ensure an explicit "no first byte" timer for the ChatGPT/Codex subscription path.
- Retry earlier when no SSE event has arrived, rather than letting a request sit for many minutes or leave the UI appearing stuck.
- Log first-byte timing and Cloudflare response metadata such as `cf-ray` when available.
- Surface this as an upstream/provider no-first-byte timeout rather than a generic task/subagent hang.

I am not posting the full request body publicly because it contains conversation/session data, but the failure is reproducible with a captured opencode request replayed directly to the Codex backend.

Duplicate of #26855 — same root cause (SSE loop race with process teardown). This issue includes a proposed fix in PR #29132.

I hit this same bug and tracked down the root cause. Submitted a fix in #29132 — the loop was called fire-and-forget (not awaited), so the process exited before the model finished generating. The fix stores the loop promise and awaits it after the prompt/command call completes.

It appears to be waiting for response indefinitely. You can interrupt (esc, esc) then resume the session by sending new message, e.g. "continue". It is much worse for sub-agent sessions obviously but you can still try to ask main agent to resume sub-agent session with the same task_id.

@chid I pushed a follow-up for the red-box case you saw.

The first patch made clipboard backend failures reject instead of being swallowed, which fixed the false `Copied to clipboard` success path. But it still was not enough: the failing native process could reject with an empty `error.message`, and a few TUI copy call sites were replacing the real error with a generic `Failed to copy` message. That is why the UI could show only a red box without useful text.

This follow-up wraps Linux clipboard backend failures with a user-facing message that names the expected dependencies (`xclip`, `xsel`, or `wl-clipboard` / `wl-copy`) and passes that message through the session copy and issue URL copy paths.

I reproduced it with a fake `xclip` that exits non-zero. Before this commit the copy rejected with an empty message; now it shows the dependency hint.

Verified:
- `bun test --timeout 30000 test/cli/cmd/tui/clipboard.test.ts`
- `bun typecheck`
- manual fake-`xclip` repro
